own_solution.law: de Broglie relation lambda = h/p with non-relativistic p = sqrt(2 m K), i.e. lambda = hc / sqrt(2 mc^2 K)
assumptions: electron starts from rest so its kinetic energy is exactly 150 eV
hc = 1240 eV nm, mc^2 = 511 keV as given

defect_reasons.other: TA9C4 and T4ACE refer to 'the proton' although the problem only mentions protons in general in a second apparatus; the referent is clear enough but the definite article is slightly loose.

notes: Base: 2 mc^2 K = 2 x 511000 x 150 = 1.533e8 eV^2, sqrt = 12381.4 eV, lambda = 1240/12381.4 = 0.10015 nm. With 90 eV added before the measurement (K = 240 eV): 2 x 511000 x 240 = 2.4528e8, sqrt = 15661.4 eV, lambda = 1240/15661.4 = 0.079176 nm. Energy added after the wavelength is determined (TB50C, T75EF) does not affect the asked value; energy given to a proton in the other apparatus (TA9C4, T4ACE) has no path to the electron. Variants: TB50C/TFC9E differ only in 'after'/'before' with the same 90 eV; TA9C4/T0058 differ only in proton/electron with the same 90 eV; T75EF and T4ACE are numeral-free versions. Non-relativistic treatment is fine at 150-240 eV (K/mc^2 < 5e-4).
